newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX hits new record of 3,813.76 points.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX hits new record of 3,813.76 points.

text.p: The Budapest bourse moved in line with slightly advancing European markets and the nearly 16 points rise pushed the BUX index to a new all-time high.
The BUX index finished at 3,813.76 points, up 15.73. The previous high of 3,803.45 points was reached on December 5.
BUX index futures firmed for five maturities and remained steady for one. December BUX ended at 3,790 points, up 24.
The resumption of trading in hotel firm Danubius shares after one day of suspension on Wednesday enhanced the market's positive sentiment.

"The market was bullish and the day's most important momentum was that one could trade in Danubius for the first time since its suspension," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securites. "This caused some euphory."

Hotelier Danubius shares surged to a new all-time high of 3,945 forints after the Competition Office (CO) had given its approval for the purchase of a hotel chain by Danubius. Later it retreated to close at 3,775 forints, up 225.

Demand was strong for Danubius between 3,700 and 3,800 forints, Berecz said, adding that "one will probably have to get accustomed to the idea of Danubius shares trading at this or even higher price levels".
Another issue highly in focus was oil and gas company MOL with over half a million shares traded.
"We are still waiting for details of the energy price increase," Berecz said.
A salesman asked during the session told Reuters that the fact that ABN AMRO Hoare Govett gave a "sell" rating to MOL this morning was only one reason behind the fall.
"What I would say is that the market is rather divided about the size of the wholesale gas price increase," the salesman said.
Elsewhere on the market both chemicals stocks hit new life highs.
Borsodchem peaked at 3,850 forints in modest turnover. It closed at 3,850, up 100.
TVK, for which CS First Boston on Wednesday said it maintained its "buy" recommendation, jumped to a new high of 1,680 forints, before closing at 1,650, up 15.
